back: $P(A) \times P(B \mid A)$ — multiply along the branches.
$P(A) + P(B) - P(A \text{ and } B)$ — add, then subtract the overlap.

front: What does "without replacement" tell you about two events?
back: They're dependent — the second pick's probabilities change because one item is now missing.

front: What does "with replacement" tell you about two events?
back: They're independent — the probabilities stay the same for every pick.

front: Quickest way to find P(at least one success)?
back: $1 - P(\text{none})$ — usually much quicker than adding up every other outcome.

front: On a tree diagram, what do the branches from the same point always add up to?
back: 1 (the probabilities of all outcomes at that point).

front: How do you find the probability of an outcome that can happen more than one way (e.g. "exactly one red")?
back: Find each path that gives that outcome, multiply along each path, then add the paths together.
